The type of the outcome variable $Y$ largely determines which regression model we use (@tbl-outcome-types).

::: {#tbl-outcome-types}

| Outcome | Examples | Analysis |
|---|---|---|
| [binary](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-binary-var) | diseased/not; died/survived | [logistic regression](logistic-regression.qmd#def-logistic-regression) |
| [count](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-count) | number of infections per month; number of follow-up visits per patient | Poisson regression |
| time to event | time from exposure until disease onset; time from onset until recurrence; time from disease onset until disease progression; time from onset until death | survival analysis |
| [ordered levels](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-ordinal-var)^[Time permitting.] | pain level (0 to 10 scale); approval rating (0 to 5 stars) | ordinal regression |

Outcome types, examples, and the regression analyses that match them
:::
